outreachTargets.pitchSubject: Data: Why workers moving NY to London face an 18% purchasing power deficit
outreachTargets.pitchAngle: Empirical relocation gap analysis comparing statutory tax brackets and rent benchmarks.
outreachTargets.pitchBody:
Hi Rachel,

Enjoyed your recent columns on mid-career relocation decisions. With professionals increasingly weighing inter-city transfers, we analyzed the exact mathematical break-even thresholds across premier corridors using verified 2026 statutory tax and HUD/ONS housing data.

Our finding: Moving from New York to London requires an 18% compensatory gross salary markup to maintain equivalent purchasing power, driven by higher UK higher-rate income tax and NHS surcharges. Conversely, moving London to Dubai yields a 12% gross discount break-even due to 0% personal income tax.

Full methodology and dataset: https://www.livworthy.com/reports/relocation-salary-gap

Happy to share the underlying spreadsheets if helpful for future reporting.
outreachTargets.notes: Verified columnist covering career transitions and work economics.

outreachTargets.pitchSubject: New Data: What a $100K salary is actually worth across 15 global metros after taxes & rent
outreachTargets.pitchAngle: Global Salary Worth Index measuring uncommitted savings capacity on $100K equivalent.
outreachTargets.pitchBody:
Hi Claire,

Following your coverage on how six-figure earners navigate living costs in high-tax metros, we published the 2026 Global Salary Worth Index analyzing true net disposable income across 15 world hubs.

Key finding: In New York City, 4 statutory deductions (Federal, NY State, NYC Resident, FICA) consume 29.1% of a $100k salary, leaving $5,907/mo. After HUD median rent ($2,655) and essential living, uncommitted savings is just 24%—compared to 51% in Dubai and 42% in Zurich.

Full interactive study and CSV export: https://www.livworthy.com/reports/global-salary-worth-index

Let me know if you would like custom data cuts for upcoming stories.
outreachTargets.notes: Active personal finance reporter covering wealth, inflation, and lifestyle affordability.

Hi Alice,

With Dubai continuing to attract international professionals, our research team published the 2026 Global Take-Home Pay Comparison analyzing net retention on a standardized $100,000 USD equivalent salary across 10 verified tax jurisdictions.
